messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Question about applying minDeltaTime by group size
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Question about applying minDeltaTime by group size
messages.body_plain:
Hello and apologies for the late reply. This is already possible. In recordTable, see the function parameters
eventSummaryColumn and eventSummaryFunction.
With these, you can specify a column in the record table (derived from the image metadata) and a function to apply to the values of that column for all records within an event. So if for example if you assign a metadata tag "n_individuals" in digiKam, you could return the maximum of " n_individuals" at each event (60 minutes or whatever you choose) . So each independent record that is retained has that summary statistic value assigned, derived from all non-independent records that are represented by that one independent record.

Hope this helps.
Best regards,
Jürgen

On Tue, Oct 28, 2025, 12:13 Ian Barbe <iann...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Jürgen, how are you?
>
> What do you think is the best strategy to apply minDeltaTime for the same species while considering the event with the largest group size?
> For example, if I detect one puma and then, 40 minutes later, two individuals, applying a 60-minute threshold would result in only one detection being counted.
>
> I was thinking that perhaps the best option would be to run minDeltaTime = 0 first and then apply a custom code to handle those cases afterwards.
>
> What do you think? Are you considering implementing something like this in future versions of camtrapR?
>
> Thank you very much for everything!
>
> Best,
> IanB
>

messages.body_plain:
I'm sorry for your trouble with this. Recently I discovered a small bug that may be related to this issue (here <https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/commit/eadfde8ab8fad1ce8e2ae6c0477a437340ca9d4e>).
If possible please download the dev version from github again and try rerunning it.
If it still fails you could try the test suite for surveyReport (in Rstudio, open the file, click "Run tests" above the source panel). This may require creating a new RStudio project from the camtrapR Github repository. This is the relevant file:
tests/testthat/test-surveyReport.R <https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/blob/dev/tests/testthat/test-surveyReport.R>

If that dosn't help please share details on the data set (like the output of str()) and the surveyReport() calls.
All the best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: # A Small Shiny App Built with camtrapR – Feedback Welcome
messages.subject_clean: # A Small Shiny App Built with camtrapR – Feedback Welcome
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I hope it’s okay to share this here. I’ve been working on a small Shiny app built around the camtrapR workflow to support National Park staff with camera-trap data management.

It’s still simple and under active development, but if anyone is interested or has suggestions, the repository is here:
https://github.com/ariefalpinus/npnameyrapp

I’d like to sincerely thank Jürgen Niedballa and the camtrapR community for creating such a great toolkit and for the ongoing development work (including the upcoming dashboard).
I would be grateful for any feedback or suggestions from the group.

Best regards,
Arief
